title: Greedy Best-First sprints through Valencia streets!
description: Watch Greedy Best-First race across a real street-map graph in Valencia (Ciutat Vella). It always expands the node that looks closest to the goal, creating fast—but sometimes imperfect—routes.
ig_caption:
⚡️ Greedy Best-First in Valencia (Ciutat Vella) 🚦

Imagine the city as a graph: intersections are nodes, streets are weighted edges (or uniform-cost edges for quick previews). Greedy Best-First uses a heuristic h(n) (like straight-line distance to the destination) and picks the next node with the *lowest* h(n) from a priority queue—so it feels like a smart “shortcut hunter.”

📍 What you’re seeing:
✅ Fast exploration toward the goal (because it trusts the heuristic)
⚠️ Potential for detours when the heuristic misleads (it doesn’t systematically guarantee the shortest path)

🧠 Under the hood:
Greedy Best-First is a best-first graph search that prioritizes promise, not proven optimality—great for responsive navigation demos and visual intuition-building.

fb_caption:
🚀 Greedy Best-First searching Valencia’s streets (Ciutat Vella)!

In graph theory terms, we convert real roads into a graph (nodes = intersections, edges = streets) and run a best-first search guided by a heuristic estimate of distance-to-go. Greedy Best-First expands the most “goal-looking” node first, which often feels quick and intuitive—even if it may not always find the absolute shortest route.

Watch how the algorithm “hunts” for the destination fast—then see where heuristic-driven choices can lead to non-optimal routes.
